The spread of agriculture — farming — was one of the most important changes in human history. Before farming, people were hunters and gatherers who moved from place to place following food. When people learned to grow crops, they could stay in one place. Permanent settlements grew into villages. Villages grew into towns and cities. Because cities needed organization, governments and laws developed. Writing was invented to keep records. In this way, farming made civilization possible.

Describe the full chain of events that the article says led from farming to civilization.

steps: Farming allowed people to stay in one place.
Permanent settlements formed.
Settlements grew into towns and cities.
Cities needed organization, so governments and laws developed.
Writing was invented to keep records.
All of this together created civilization.
solution.answer: Farming allowed people to stay in one place, which led to permanent settlements that grew into cities. Cities needed governments and laws, and writing was invented to keep records. Together, these developments led to civilization.

The discovery of DNA's structure in 1953 by Watson and Crick changed science forever. Before this discovery, scientists did not know how traits were passed from parents to children. Because scientists could now study DNA, they understood inheritance at a molecular level. Over the following decades, this knowledge led to new medical treatments, the ability to identify people from a drop of blood, and the mapping of the entire human genome.

Identify the central discovery described and explain how it connects to the developments that followed it.

steps: The central discovery: the structure of DNA in 1953.
Because scientists understood DNA, they could study how traits are inherited.
This led to new medical treatments.
It also led to DNA identification techniques.
It led to mapping the human genome.
solution.answer: The central discovery was DNA's structure in 1953. Because scientists now understood DNA, they could study inheritance, which led to medical breakthroughs, DNA identification, and the mapping of the human genome.

In 1815, the volcano Mount Tambora erupted in Indonesia — the most powerful eruption in recorded history. So much ash was thrown into the atmosphere that it blocked sunlight around the world. Because less sunlight reached crops, 1816 became known as 'The Year Without a Summer.' Harvests failed across Europe and North America. Widespread food shortages caused prices to rise sharply. Thousands of people died of starvation, and many families were forced to migrate to new regions.

Describe the step-by-step connection between the volcanic eruption and people being forced to migrate.

steps: Eruption threw ash into the atmosphere.
Ash blocked sunlight worldwide.
Less sunlight caused crop failures.
Crop failures caused food shortages.
Food shortages raised prices.
Starvation and high prices forced people to migrate.
solution.answer: The eruption threw ash into the atmosphere that blocked sunlight. Less sunlight caused crops to fail, leading to food shortages. Food shortages caused starvation and high prices, which forced thousands of people to migrate.

The internet changed the way people find information. Before the internet, if you wanted to research a topic, you had to go to a library and look through books and encyclopedias, which could take hours. Because the internet lets people search for information instantly, research that once took days can now be done in minutes. As a result, students, scientists, and workers can learn and solve problems much faster than before. However, the internet also means that incorrect information spreads faster too.

Explain how the internet changed research for both better and worse, based on the cause-and-effect information in the passage.

steps: Before: research required going to a library and searching for hours.
The internet allows instant searching, so research takes minutes instead of days.
Better: faster learning and problem-solving.
Worse: incorrect information also spreads faster.
solution.answer: The internet made research faster by allowing people to search instantly instead of spending hours in libraries. This helped students and scientists learn and solve problems more quickly. However, the same speed also means incorrect information spreads faster — both a benefit and a problem.

When oil spills into the ocean, the effects spread far beyond where the spill happened. Oil floats on the surface and coats the feathers of seabirds, preventing them from flying or staying warm. Because seabirds cannot fly, they cannot hunt and often starve. Oil also settles on the ocean floor, smothering sea creatures and coral reefs. The effects can last for decades because oil decomposes very slowly in cold seawater.

Describe the connection the article makes between oil coating seabirds' feathers and seabird deaths.

steps: Oil coats seabirds' feathers.
Coated feathers prevent seabirds from flying and staying warm.
Because they cannot fly, seabirds cannot hunt.
Unable to hunt, they often starve.
solution.answer: Oil coats seabirds' feathers, which prevents them from flying or staying warm. Because they cannot fly, they cannot hunt for food, so they often starve.

The transistor, invented in 1947, made modern computers possible. Before transistors, computers used large, power-hungry vacuum tubes to process information. Because transistors were small and used little power, computers could be made much smaller and cheaper. As transistors became even smaller, computers shrank from room-sized machines to desktop computers to smartphones. Today, a smartphone contains billions of transistors.

Trace the connection from the invention of the transistor to smartphones.

steps: Before transistors: computers used large vacuum tubes and were room-sized.
Transistors were smaller and used less power.
This allowed computers to be made smaller and cheaper.
As transistors shrank further, computers moved from desks to pockets.
Today smartphones contain billions of transistors.
solution.answer: Transistors replaced large vacuum tubes, allowing computers to become smaller and cheaper. As transistors continued to shrink, computers shrank too, eventually fitting in our pockets as smartphones, which today contain billions of transistors.

The black plague swept through Europe in the 1300s and killed about one third of the population. Because so many workers died, farms and workshops were left with fewer laborers. The surviving workers could demand higher wages because they were scarce. Some historians believe that the resulting rise in wages helped break down the feudal system, in which poor farmers were bound to work on a lord's land for little pay. In this unexpected way, a deadly disease helped lead to economic change.

Explain the indirect connection the article describes between the black plague and the weakening of the feudal system.

steps: The plague killed about one third of the population.
Fewer workers meant farms and workshops were shorthanded.
Surviving workers could demand higher wages because they were scarce.
Higher wages helped break down the feudal system that kept workers poor.
solution.answer: The plague killed so many workers that those who survived became scarce and could demand higher wages. Higher wages undermined the feudal system, which depended on cheap, bound labor — so a deadly disease indirectly contributed to economic change.

When a keystone species is removed from an ecosystem, the entire system can collapse. A keystone species is one whose impact is much larger than its numbers suggest. Sea otters are a keystone species. They eat sea urchins, keeping their population in check. Sea urchins eat kelp. When sea otters were hunted nearly to extinction in the 1800s, sea urchin populations exploded. The urchins ate so much kelp that the kelp forests disappeared. Many fish, seals, and eagles lost their habitat and food source. Removing one species caused an entire ecosystem to unravel.

Describe the full cause-and-effect chain that resulted from the hunting of sea otters.

steps: Sea otters were hunted to near extinction.
Without otters, sea urchin populations exploded.
Urchins ate enormous amounts of kelp.
Kelp forests disappeared.
Fish, seals, and eagles lost their habitat and food source.
solution.answer: Hunting sea otters to near extinction caused sea urchin populations to explode. The urchins ate so much kelp that kelp forests disappeared. Without kelp forests, fish, seals, and eagles lost their habitat and food, causing the entire ecosystem to unravel.

In the 1800s, John Snow solved a deadly mystery in London. Cholera was killing hundreds of people, and no one knew why. Snow mapped where each case of cholera occurred. He noticed that almost all the sick people lived near one water pump on Broad Street. When the pump handle was removed so people could not use the water, the outbreak slowed. His detective work proved that contaminated water caused cholera, not bad air as people believed. This discovery changed medicine by showing that diseases could spread through water.

Describe the connection between John Snow's mapping of cholera cases and the discovery that water spread disease.

steps: Snow mapped cholera cases and noticed they clustered near one water pump.
He removed the pump handle to test his theory.
The outbreak slowed after the pump was disabled.
This proved contaminated water, not bad air, caused cholera.
The discovery changed medicine's understanding of how diseases spread.
solution.answer: By mapping cholera cases, Snow noticed they clustered near one water pump. Removing the pump handle slowed the outbreak, proving that contaminated water caused cholera. This changed medicine by showing that diseases can spread through water.

The wolf reintroduction in Yellowstone National Park in 1995 had surprising effects. Before wolves returned, elk herds grazed freely everywhere, eating so many streamside plants that riverbanks eroded. When wolves arrived, elk avoided open areas near streams where they could be caught. Because elk no longer grazed the streamside plants, willows and aspens grew back. Tree roots held the soil, and riverbanks stopped eroding. Beavers returned to build dams, and the dams created ponds that attracted fish, ducks, and otters. Wolves changed not just animal populations but the physical landscape of the park.

Explain how the return of wolves to Yellowstone changed the rivers and streams of the park.

steps: Wolves caused elk to avoid streamside areas.
Without elk grazing, streamside plants grew back.
Plant roots held the soil and stopped riverbank erosion.
Beavers returned and built dams.
Dams created ponds that attracted fish and other animals.
solution.answer: When wolves returned, elk avoided streams, allowing streamside plants to grow back. The plants' roots stopped riverbank erosion. Beavers returned and built dams, creating ponds that attracted fish, ducks, and otters. Wolves indirectly restored the health of the rivers.

The assembly line, perfected by Henry Ford in the early 1900s, transformed manufacturing. Before assembly lines, workers built one complete product from start to finish. This took a long time and required each worker to know many skills. With an assembly line, each worker did only one small task repeatedly. Because tasks were simple and repeated, workers could be trained quickly. The speed of production increased dramatically, and because more cars could be made, the price per car dropped. As a result, ordinary families who could never afford a car before could now buy one.

Describe the connection between the assembly line and ordinary families being able to afford cars.

steps: Assembly line simplified tasks, so workers could be trained quickly.
Simple, repeated tasks increased the speed of production.
More cars produced meant lower price per car.
Lower prices meant ordinary families could afford to buy cars.
solution.answer: The assembly line simplified and sped up production, allowing more cars to be made. More cars being made lowered the price of each car, which meant ordinary families who could not previously afford a car could now buy one.

Salt was one of the most valuable substances in the ancient world. Before refrigeration, salt was the main way to preserve food. Because salt was so essential, it was traded along major routes across Africa, Europe, and Asia. Some ancient trade routes were so important that they became roads, which connected cities and allowed ideas, languages, and goods to spread. The Roman word for soldier's pay was 'salarium,' meaning salt payment — the origin of our modern word 'salary.'

Describe the connection between salt's role in food preservation and the development of trade routes.

steps: Salt was essential for food preservation before refrigeration.
Because salt was so essential, it became a valuable trade good.
Salt was traded along major routes across continents.
Those routes eventually became roads that connected cities.
Roads allowed the spread of ideas, languages, and goods.
solution.answer: Salt was essential for preserving food, making it extremely valuable. Because it was so valuable, salt was traded widely, creating important trade routes. Those routes became roads that connected cities and spread ideas and goods across continents.

Conservation efforts saved the American alligator from extinction. By the 1960s, alligators had been heavily hunted for their skin, and their numbers had fallen sharply. In 1967, alligators were listed as an endangered species, and hunting was banned. Because hunting stopped and their habitat was protected, alligator populations recovered dramatically. By 1987, they were removed from the endangered list. Today, alligators play a key role in their wetland ecosystems by digging holes that other animals use for water during droughts.

Describe the step-by-step connection between hunting bans and alligators helping other animals.

steps: Alligators were heavily hunted and became endangered.
Hunting was banned in 1967 and habitat was protected.
Because of the ban, alligator populations recovered.
Recovered alligators dig holes in wetlands.
Other animals use those holes for water during droughts.
solution.answer: After hunting bans protected alligators, their populations recovered. Recovered alligators dug holes in wetlands that other animals use for water during droughts, so conservation efforts benefited not just alligators but the entire ecosystem.

Maps have changed dramatically because of satellites. Before GPS satellites existed, sailors and travelers used paper maps and compasses to navigate. Because paper maps could be outdated or hard to read, travelers sometimes got lost. GPS satellites orbit Earth and continuously send location signals. Devices on the ground receive those signals and calculate their exact position in seconds. As a result, GPS navigation is accurate to within a few feet, and drivers, hikers, and pilots rarely get lost today.

Describe the connection between GPS satellites and the reduction in people getting lost.

steps: Before GPS, paper maps could be outdated and hard to read, causing people to get lost.
GPS satellites orbit Earth and send continuous location signals.
Devices receive those signals and calculate exact positions in seconds.
Because GPS is accurate to within a few feet, people rarely get lost today.
solution.answer: GPS satellites send continuous location signals that devices use to calculate exact positions. Because GPS is accurate to within a few feet and updates in real time, it replaced unreliable paper maps and greatly reduced how often people get lost.

The construction of the Transcontinental Railroad, completed in 1869, transformed the United States. Before the railroad, traveling from New York to California took six months by wagon or three weeks by ship around South America. The railroad reduced the trip to about a week. Because travel was faster, people moved west in large numbers. Towns grew along the railroad route. The railroad made it possible to ship cattle and wheat from the west to cities in the east, creating a national economy. Native American communities suffered deeply, as the railroad brought settlers onto their lands.

Describe at least two effects the Transcontinental Railroad had on the United States, according to the article.

steps: Effect 1: Travel time from New York to California dropped from months to about a week.
Effect 2: More people moved west, and towns grew along the railroad.
Effect 3: Cattle and wheat could be shipped east, creating a national economy.
Effect 4: Native American communities suffered as settlers moved onto their lands.
solution.answer: The Transcontinental Railroad dramatically reduced travel time from months to about a week, which caused more people to move west and towns to grow along the route. It also created a national economy by allowing cattle and wheat to be shipped east. However, it also brought settlers onto Native American lands, causing great suffering for those communities.
